title: The command line reads the product's configuration
description: `lathe check` calls `loadWorkspace` on the product root, which reads `lathe.config.json`: its one setting, the data folder.

title: The store loads every data file into the typed tables
description: The store reads each `data/<table>.jsonl`, and Lathe's `lathe/data/check.jsonl` beside them, checks each row's columns and types, inserts the tables in dependency order in one transaction and runs the validation queries. A load it refuses becomes `data-refused` errors naming the file, the line and the rule, and the check stops there.
transaction_name: the load, on a fresh in-memory database
statements: one INSERT per table, or per level of a self-referencing table, then the validation queries

title: The engine fills the file facts and creates the coverage views
description: Each test's and component's file is read into `file_facts` and `file_mentions`, then the coverage views are created over the typed tables, so every check and the coverage counts read the same facts.
statements: two CREATE TABLE for the facts with their rows appended, then one CREATE VIEW per coverage view

title: The checks read the product's settings from product_setting
description: Nothing is written for the settings: `product_setting` is a typed table like any other, and a check reads `max_children` from it, 15 when the product has no row.

title: Lathe's checks run in position order, then the product's own
description: Each check row is one SELECT over the same tables, returning `record` and `message` (and `severity` when its rows say which); a product's check reports only on records of its product.
statements: one SELECT per check row, on up to four connections side by side

title: Coverage is counted per domain and obligation kind
description: Designed, built, proved and planned are read for every obligation kind in every domain from the coverage views, with the gaps and the tests by state.
statements: the coverage counts, gaps and tests-by-state queries over the views

title: The command prints the report and sets the exit status
description: Errors are printed first, then warnings, then a coverage line per domain and obligation kind; the exit status is 1 when there is an error.

title: With --json, the command prints the whole workspace instead
description: After the same load, `--json` prints the `Workspace` as JSON in place of the text report.
